## `cargo_interior_merge_pipeline.md`

---

---
name: cargo_interior_merge_pipeline
description: Cargo shell interior features are merged by merge_cargo_interior.py; MESH-01 root cause was sequential trimesh booleans; SCAD GPS/FPV/servo/latch/avionics modules are in a broken legacy frame
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: aff049a4-06f0-42ee-bea6-0de2d216a4fc
---

The **cargo** fuselage shell is produced by `airframe/blender-scripts/merge_cargo_interior.py`
(Rev R1, 2026-06-30), NOT by `add_structural_features.py` (which now SKIPs cargo). It starts
from the clean Blender source, bakes to hull frame, and merges every cargo interior feature in
ONE `(shell + positives) − negatives` manifold3d expression. Output:
`airframe/stls/fuselage/cargo/cargo_sect_shell24_2mm_repaired.stl` — watertight, single body,
vol ≈ 323 188 mm³.

**MESH-01 root cause (fixed 2026-06-30):** it was NOT mainly the cutter-vs-wall epsilon; it was
`add_structural_features._subtract_all` subtracting cutters ONE AT A TIME via
`trimesh.boolean.difference(engine="manifold")` + per-step repair on a 1.4 M-face shell, which
compounded slivers into 10⁴+ bodies. Fix = union ALL cutters into one Manifold, do a SINGLE
difference (boolean of closed manifolds is closed ⇒ watertight out). Cutting a through-aperture
with a solid box keeps the mesh watertight (it becomes an open "cup" — still a closed 2-manifold).

**GOTCHA — the cargo SCAD interior modules are in a BROKEN legacy mental frame.** Only the WING +
nacelle-servo modules in `cargo_sect_shell24.scad` were reconciled to true hull frame (Rev R1
2026-06-22). The **GPS, FPV, door-servo-pad, latch-lip, and avionics-bay (Inara/River) modules
were authored with X=longitudinal, Y=vertical/dorsal, Z=lateral** — so `AVINICS_DORSAL_Y` etc. do
NOT map to correct hull positions through the bake transform (they'd land on the fwd joint face,
not the dorsal top). These were DEFERRED in the merge and must be RE-DERIVED in hull frame before
cutting the dorsal access panel / skin recesses. See [[project_r1_hull_frame_bake]].

Wing spar/mortise Y was re-derived (129 mm Rev R1 chord, LE root hull Y=−7 → spar 30% Y=+31.7,
mortise 50% Y=+57.5), superseding the stale-161 mm `WING_ROOT_Y_CEN=CY+40`. Lateral-wall/dorsal
features are seated against the mesh-sampled wall (walls curve inboard with Z; bbox extremity
floats off). Aft door hinge retention blocks (hull Y +109..+121) sit only ~9 mm from the aft
landing-leg row (Y≈100) — leg bosses must clear them.

## `env_kiutils_missing.md`

---

---
name: env_kiutils_missing
description: kiutils is NOT installed and pip is not permitted, so the KiCad generator scripts in Open-Secure-ESC cannot run; extend schematics by injection instead
metadata:
  type: reference
---

`kiutils` is not installed anywhere on this machine and pip installs are not
permitted. That means **none of the Open-Secure-ESC generators can run**:
`symbols/tools/gen_kicad_symbol.py`, `builds/.../kicad/tools/gen_schematic.py`,
`gen_pcb.py`, and `genlib.py` all import it and fail at module load.

Consequences, learned 2026-08-10:

- To change a schematic, write a **targeted S-expression injection script**
  that only appends objects (see
  `builds/6s/50A/CAN_485_faraday/kicad/tools/inject_optiga_secure_element.py`
  and `LibreServo_v4/PCB/kicad/tools/swap_slb9672_for_optiga.py`). Commit the
  script so the edit stays auditable.
- Never "fix" generator drift by writing placement code you cannot execute —
  `gen_schematic.py` now carries a divergence warning instead, because
  unverified generator code that silently overwrites a verified schematic is
  the exact failure AGENTS.md §1.3 guards against.
- To keep a `.kicad_sym` in sync with its `specs/*.json` twin, hand-sync only
  the text properties; leave pin/graphic geometry alone.
- Validate every hand edit with `kicad-cli` 9.0.2: `sch erc --severity-all`,
  `sch export netlist`, `sym export svg`. Record the before/after ERC counts —
  ERC "Failed to load schematic" is how a malformed S-expression shows up.

Parser trap: don't locate the end of an embedded `lib_symbol` by matching
`\t\t\t)\n\t\t)` — there is an `(embedded_fonts no)` line before the close, so
the pattern silently matches somewhere else far down the file. Walk parens.

Related: [[project_optiga_trust_m_swap]], [[env_venv_hides_system_python]],
[[feedback_generator_drift_and_freerouting]]

## `env_openfoam_airfoil_meshing.md`

---

---
name: env_openfoam_airfoil_meshing
description: "OpenFOAM v1912 works on this box, but hand-rolled blockMesh O-grids for S1223 will not reach zero inverted cells — six approaches recorded"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: f91efc1e-e301-4097-85ce-3de1beddb631
  modified: 2026-08-16T11:47:02.253Z
---

OpenFOAM **v1912** is installed via Debian packages (`/usr/bin/simpleFoam`,
`blockMesh`, `snappyHexMesh`, `checkMesh`). Source it with
`. /usr/share/openfoam/etc/bashrc` — running the binaries without that fails
with "Could not find mandatory etc entry 'controlDict'".

The solver side is easy; **meshing a thin, strongly cambered aerofoil (S1223) by
hand in blockMesh is not**. Attempted 2026-08-16 and abandoned at 2–4 inverted
quads out of 48 000 — blockMesh rejects the mesh, so no results were produced.
Do not retry these (all measured):

- one-block-per-quadrant O-grid, straight radial interpolation → 634 negative
  cells, skewness 5866 (blockMesh interpolates linearly between a block's inner
  and outer edges; straight lines from the section to a circle cross near the TE)
- far ring mapped by angle about quarter-chord → rays fold, because S1223's
  lower surface rises **above the chord line aft of ~8% chord**, so (0.25, 0) is
  not inside the section
- far ring mapped by angle about the polygon centroid → still non-monotonic
- global Laplacian relaxation of interior rings → equalises radial spacing, so
  boundary-layer clustering washes out and near-wall rings tangle; layer grading
  comes out < 1 (contracting outward)
- uniform arclength redistribution of each marched ring → shears the radial
  correspondence, 7630 inverted
- parameter sweeps over normal smoothing, TE bluntness, blend power, first-cell
  height, circumferential count, plus local untangling → floor is 2–4

What did help: ray-projecting the **marched** ring onto the far circle instead of
a fixed arclength→angle map (7126 → 41), ~100 circumferential blocks (blockMesh
validates a block from its 8 CORNER vertices, not its polyLine edges, so a long
block is judged on a chord that cuts through the section), and wall-function
near-wall spacing rather than y+≈1 (aspect ratio ~1000 is what makes marching
ill-conditioned).

Next time use elliptic grid generation with orthogonality control, or a C-grid
(better suited to a cusped TE than an O-grid), or snappyHexMesh — but a 2D
snappy case needs a `refineMesh`-based workflow so refinement does not split the
empty direction.

Harness lives at `tools/wing_cfd_openfoam.py`, committed WIP with all of the
above in its docstring. Related: [[project_wing_spar_rev_s1b]],
[[env_venv_hides_system_python]] (use `/usr/bin/python3`).

## `env_venv_hides_system_python.md`

---

---
name: env-venv-hides-system-python
description: "Serenity .venv has include-system-site-packages=false, hiding manifold3d/sympy/matplotlib; run mesh-boolean tooling with /usr/bin/python3 (pip is not permitted on this system)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 41ad9868-1d22-4161-8ca1-2dea4ad112a0
  modified: 2026-08-09T13:50:55.155Z
---

`<repo>/.venv` is auto-activated (`VIRTUAL_ENV` is set, so a bare `python3` is
the venv interpreter) and was created with `include-system-site-packages =
false`. That hides packages which ARE installed on this machine, so an import
check inside the venv reports them missing and looks like a blocker:

| package | venv | where it actually lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `manifold3d` | missing | `~/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/` (user site — venvs disable user site entirely, so `include-system-site-packages=true` alone would NOT expose it) |
| `sympy` 1.13.3 | missing | apt `python3-sympy` → `/usr/lib/python3/dist-packages` |
| `matplotlib` 3.10.1 | missing | apt `python3-matplotlib` → same |
| `numpy`/`scipy`/`trimesh` | present | both places (venv newer: numpy 2.5.1 / scipy 1.18.0) |

**pip is not permitted on this system.** Do not propose `pip install` as the
fix — nothing needs installing.

**Fix: run the affected script with `/usr/bin/python3`, not `python3`.**
Verified that the whole `airframe/blender-scripts/merge_cargo_interior.py`
import graph (numpy, trimesh, manifold3d, `add_structural_features`,
`generate_cargo_hinge_retention`) resolves under `/usr/bin/python3`, and that a
real `Manifold` boolean evaluates. This matters because that script is the
definitive cargo-section processor and cannot run at all without manifold3d —
see [[cargo_interior_merge_pipeline]].

Also absent everywhere and NOT needed: `pint`. Use `sympy.physics.units`
instead (it carries `pound`/`newton`, so it covers the lbm/lbf discipline
AGENTS.md mandates).

`rtree` and `embree` are absent too, which disables `trimesh.ray.*` and
`trimesh.proximity.closest_point`. Projection or sectioning against mesh
vertices is the workaround — see [[project_landing_gear_bay_conforming]].

## `feedback_gates_mask_tool_bugs.md`

---

---
name: feedback_gates_mask_tool_bugs
description: When a gate is red for a known geometry reason, its OTHER checks are unvalidated — fixing the geometry exposes tool bugs, so budget for them
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Serenity-UAV, 2026-08-30. `wing_root_deconflict.py` had been red "by design"
since Rev T1 for one known cause. Fixing that cause exposed **four** genuine
defects in the checkers that the red state had been hiding:

- `tenon_params()` matched only `"two_rod"`, so the Rev T1 default path
  `"spar_carrythrough"` fell through to the **enlarged 30 mm tenon** — reporting
  an 8.60 mm/side mortise foul against a correctly-sized mortise. The SCAD writes
  the rule as a *negative* (`!= "enlarged_tenon"`) precisely so new paths inherit
  the safe size; the tool mirrored it as a positive whitelist and inverted it.
- The spar corridor is **stepped** (Ø20.4 outboard, Ø16.3 inboard) and was swept
  at one diameter, reading the intended annulus as "wall not cut".
- Every route was probed 12 mm past the wall bracket — right for a rigid shaft,
  wrong for a wire that turns.
- `cargo_bay_envelope.py` derived spar OD with the retired 0.15 mm/side rotating
  clearance and printed "rotating tilt-spar" for a fixed bonded tube.

**Why:** a failing gate is not a *partially* passing gate. Everything downstream
of the first failure is unexercised, and stale assumptions accumulate there
undisturbed.

**How to apply:** when clearing a long-red gate, expect to fix the gate too;
read each check's assumptions against the *current* design before trusting a new
green. Related: [[project_fuselage_rev_t1c_tilt_drive]].

## `feedback_generator_drift_and_freerouting.md`

---

---
name: feedback_generator_drift_and_freerouting
description: "When a board's gen_*.py no longer reproduces the checked-in .kicad_sch, inject rather than regenerate; how to autoroute via KiCad's Specctra DSN/SES bridge + freerouting"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 72cf1df7-3b8d-42f2-b896-bc45bb86ab02
  modified: 2026-07-26T22:31:24.842Z
---

**Generator drift**: before assuming a board's `gen_*.py` script is safe to re-run, diff its
output against the checked-in file's `kicad-cli sch erc` error count. Found 2026-07-26: running
Kaylee's `gen_kaylee.py` fresh from git HEAD (unmodified) produces 247 ERC errors where the real
checked-in `Kaylee.kicad_sch` has 0 — the generator had drifted from hand-tuning done at some
point in the KiCad GUI. **Why this matters**: full regeneration in this state would silently
destroy the working file. **How to apply**: when a generator has drifted, add new content via a
non-destructive text-injection script instead (parse the existing file, splice new lib_symbols/
body content in via balanced-paren-safe string insertion before the relevant closing parens, use
a distinct UUID-prefix stream to avoid collisions) — see `inject_kaylee_trust_module.py` and
`inject_emma_tpm.py` in `avionics/kicad/*/scripts/` for the working pattern. Re-verify by running
`kicad-cli sch erc` on the injected result.

**Also**: once the user has done manual PCB component packing/placement in the KiCad GUI, never
re-run the PCB-generation script (e.g. `gen_*_pcb.py`) without asking first — it will silently
overwrite that manual work. Confirmed by the user 2026-07-26 after this happened once with
`gen_can_periph_gw_pcb.py`.

**Freerouting an actual board in this environment**: `kicad-cli pcb export` has no DSN
subcommand and `pcbnew.PCB_IO_MGR` exposes no DSN plugin by name — but `pcbnew.ExportSpecctraDSN
(board, dsn_path)` / `pcbnew.ImportSpecctraSES(board, ses_path)` DO exist and work (verified
2026-07-26; an earlier guess at `pcbnew.ExportSpecctraFile` does not exist). See
`tools/export-specctra-dsn.py` / `tools/import-specctra-ses.py`. The bundled freerouting native
launcher (`bin/freerouting`) hangs waiting for a GUI with no display — invoke the JAR directly
with the system `java` instead: `java -jar <freerouting-dir>/lib/app/freerouting-executable.jar
-de <in.dsn> -do <out.ses> -mp <passes>`. Do NOT hand-roll a naive MST/straight-line autorouter as
a fallback — tried once, made DRC dramatically worse (114 unconnected → 266 violations including
48 real shorts) because it has no collision avoidance.

## `feedback_ground_clearance_requirement.md`

---

---
name: feedback-ground-clearance-requirement
description: "Ground clearance on Serenity is an aircraft-safety spec only, not sized to a cargo box's height — correction after I (Claude) misinterpreted it"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8d7a83fc-067e-4887-ad99-15b4a8a6dd5c
  modified: 2026-07-26T18:16:56.822Z
---

Landing-gear ground clearance on the Serenity UAV is an **aircraft-safety
requirement only** (avoid a belly/tail strike, keep the hull clear of
ground debris during the landing/absorption stroke) — it is **not** sized
to let the parked aircraft straddle a cargo box's height. The 3×3×4 ft
cargo is carried internally; the aircraft **lands on top of** a
ground-staged cargo box with the cargo-bay doors open, then winches the
box into the bay. The gear never needs to clear the box while parked.

**Why:** I (Claude) inferred from the cargo box dimensions that the
landing gear needed enough ground clearance to fit the box underneath the
parked aircraft, and carried a ≥76 mm (3.0 in) requirement forward from
Rev R1 through Rev R6 on that basis. Steve corrected this 2026-07-23: the
real ops concept is land-over-then-winch-in, so the clearance minimum only
needs to satisfy flight safety, not cargo geometry. See
[[project_landing_gear_r6_variants]] for what changed as a result (the
1.5in/3.0in leg-length variant split in `docs/LANDING_GEAR_ANALYSIS.md`).

**How to apply:** Don't back-derive structural or geometric requirements
from a payload's physical dimensions unless the user has stated that the
payload must physically pass through/under/around that geometry. When a
requirement traces to "cargo needs to fit here," verify the actual
loading/unloading concept of operations first — on this project, cargo is
frequently handled by winching, docking, or other non-clearance methods
rather than physical pass-through.

## `feedback_kicad_hand_authoring.md`

---

---
name: feedback_kicad_hand_authoring
description: "Hand-authoring .kicad_sch — pin transform is instance_pos + Rot(angle)·(lib_x,−lib_y) at ANY angle; no ';' comments; verify by node count; kicad-cli version must match generator_version"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 0b104538-4478-49ff-91a6-9f2a40e2e90a
  modified: 2026-08-24T12:54:34.839Z
---

When hand-authoring KiCad schematics (`.kicad_sch` S-expr), a placed symbol's pins land
at **sheet = instance_pos + Rot(instance_angle) · (lib_x, −lib_y)** — the Y offset is
**always negated before the rotation is applied**, at every rotation angle, not just 0°.
X is never negated on its own. (Previously recorded as "sheet_y = instance_y − lib_y";
that was only the angle-0 special case of this general rule. Confirmed again on the
osc-sg90-v006 ECC204 addition: an `angle 0` GND pin still needed the Y-negation — I
assumed angle-0 meant no transform at all and got it backwards, caught by
`pin_not_connected`/`power_pin_not_driven` on ERC/DRC after fixing the same bug I'd
already recorded here once.)

**Why:** I wired instance pins using `+lib_y` and silently **cross-wired every multi-pin
part**. Symmetric parts (a 4-pin pigtail, a 2-terminal R/C) still pass `kicad-cli` ERC
with 0 errors while being wrong, because the wrong pin still lands on a valid net by
symmetry — only asymmetric parts (the AK7455, or a mis-netted GND/power pin) expose it.
ERC error count alone does NOT prove correct connectivity; a power pin landing on the
wrong coordinate self-reports as its own isolated net (`pin_not_connected` +
`power_pin_not_driven`), which is the actual tell.

**How to apply:**
- Compute each pin's sheet coord as `instance_pos + Rot(angle) · (lib_x, −lib_y)`; for
  angle 0 that's `(instance_x + lib_x, instance_y − lib_y)`, for angle 180 it's
  `(instance_x − lib_x, instance_y + lib_y)` — verified against this repo's own already-
  wired symbols (SWDIO label sitting exactly on a pin) before trusting it on new work.
- Pick instance placement coordinates that are themselves multiples of the pin-offset
  grid (1.27 mm in this repo) — every pin offset is already an N×1.27 multiple, so a
  grid-aligned instance center guarantees every derived pin lands on-grid too, avoiding a
  wall of `endpoint_off_grid` warnings.
- Verify with `kicad-cli sch export netlist` and check **each net's node count** (e.g. a
  point-to-point signal must be 2 nodes), not just the ERC error total.
- KiCad's parser **rejects `;` semicolon comments** — do not put them in `.kicad_sch`
  (they cause "Failed to load schematic"). Use `(text …)` notes instead.
- Add `PWR_FLAG` on externally-supplied rails (pigtail-fed +3V3/GND) to clear
  `power_pin_not_driven`.
- **`kicad-cli`'s version must be ≥ the file's `generator_version`, or it silently fails
  to load the file at all** ("Failed to load schematic"/"Failed to load board", no other
  diagnostic) — this reproduces even on an untouched, just-committed file, so don't read
  it as a sign your edit broke something. Check the file's own
  `(generator_version "X.Y")` header first. open-servo-core-secure's boards are KiCad-10
  files (`"10.0"`); the system `kicad-cli` here is 9.0.2 and cannot load them at all. Fix:
  run the newer `kicad-cli` bundled in a KiCad 10 AppImage instead of installing a second
  system copy — `/path/to/kicad-10.0.3-x86_64.AppImage kicad-cli <normal args>` (it's a
  `sharun`-runtime AppImage: the bare AppImage prints `sharun` usage, but it dispatches
  any bundled binary name given as the first argument, so `kicad-cli` works as a
  sub-invocation without extracting or installing anything).
- Run both `sch erc` and `pcb drc` **in place**, in the real project directory, so
  `fp-lib-table`/`sym-lib-table`/`.kicad_pro` resolve — running against a copy elsewhere
  (even with those files copied alongside) inflates unrelated violations (footprint
  resolution differences) and produces a false diff. To isolate what your own edit
  introduced, `git stash` the edit, run the check in place for the baseline count, `git
  stash pop`, run it again, and diff by (violation type, item description, position) —
  do not just eyeball the totals, since even a clean baseline on a real board can carry
  dozens of pre-existing violations having nothing to do with your change.

See [[project_tilt_encoder_ak7455]], [[project_avionics_board_folder_reorg]].

## `feedback_kicad_pcb_footprint_rotation.md`

---

---
name: feedback_kicad_pcb_footprint_rotation
description: "Hand-authoring .kicad_pcb — pad transform is instance_pos + Rot(−angle)·(local, Y-negated if B.Cu); verify against live Gerber %TO.P% comments, not guesswork"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 0b104538-4478-49ff-91a6-9f2a40e2e90a
  modified: 2026-08-25T12:13:43.646Z
---

When hand-authoring KiCad **PCB** files (`.kicad_pcb` S-expr — this is a
*different* rule from schematic symbol pins, see [[feedback_kicad_hand_authoring]]),
a footprint's pad lands at **board_pos = instance_pos + Rot(−instance_angle) ·
(local_x, local_y')**, where `Rot` is the standard CCW rotation matrix and
`local_y' = −local_y` only when the footprint is on `B.Cu` (front-layer
footprints use `local_y' = local_y` unchanged). **The stored angle is negated
before rotating** — I assumed the stored angle was applied directly (standard
CCW, no negation) and got it backwards on both layers.

**Why:** I spent a full extra round of a session unable to reconcile
DRC-reported pad positions for a real, unmodified component (`J4`) against my
own hand-computed positions, and wrongly concluded DRC was reporting stale
zone-fill data or that the board had a duplicate-reference bug confusing the
tool — neither was true. The only actual bug was my own rotation formula.
Confirmed by cross-referencing a live-exported Gerber's `%TO.P,<ref>,<pin>%`
component-attribute comments (emitted immediately before each pad's `D03`
flash) against the coordinates DRC reported — direct, unambiguous ground
truth, since it's KiCad's own plotter stating "this exact flash belongs to
this exact pin." Solving for the rotation that reconciles local pin
coordinates with those confirmed absolute positions gave `Rot(−θ)`, not
`Rot(+θ)`.

**How to apply:**
- For a `B.Cu` footprint at instance angle θ: `board = instance + Rot(−θ) ·
  (local_x, −local_y)`. For `F.Cu`: `board = instance + Rot(−θ) ·
  (local_x, local_y)`.
- **Do not trust your own derivation without independent verification** —
  export a Gerber for the affected layer (`kicad-cli pcb export gerbers
  --layers <layer> -o <dir> <file>.kicad_pcb`) and grep for
  `%TO.P,<ref>,<pin_or_number>%` immediately followed by an `X..Y..D03*`
  flash. That coordinate is ground truth (note: Gerber Y is the *negative*
  of board Y — `%FSLAX46Y46%` + `board_y = -gerber_y`). Cross-check at least
  one asymmetric or known-net pad before trusting the formula on new work,
  the same way [[feedback_kicad_hand_authoring]] says to check schematic
  pins against an already-wired label.
- A footprint's declared pad `size` is not necessarily its real copper
  extent — a through-hole pad can declare a tiny `size` (e.g. `0.1mm`) with
  a much larger `drill` (e.g. `0.9mm`); KiCad enforces a minimum annular
  ring, so the effective copper is close to `drill + 2×ring`, not the
  declared `size`. Don't use the bare `size` field for clearance/placement
  math on any pad whose `drill` is close to or larger than its `size`
  — verify the real extent via the same Gerber-flash method (the aperture
  selected for the `D03` flash states the actual plotted diameter).
- **A hand-edit to only the outer `(at X Y angle)` line of a footprint is
  not sufficient if that footprint's per-pad/per-property `(at ...)` lines
  carry their own angle suffix** — KiCad stores the same rotation angle
  redundantly on the outer footprint line *and* on every pad/property
  `(at x y angle)` line inside it, and a GUI "move" (as opposed to
  "rotate") can desync them (flatten the inner ones to 0 while leaving the
  outer line correct). The result parses fine and looks fine but produces
  wrong absolute pad positions and cascading, hard-to-trace DRC findings
  against unrelated nearby components. After any edit to a rotated
  footprint, diff its *entire* block against a known-good copy (e.g.
  `git show HEAD:<file>` for the same UUID), not just the position line —
  or replace the whole block wholesale rather than patching one line.
- Whether `kicad-cli pcb drc`/`pcb export gerbers` read a zone's *live
  recomputed* fill or its *stored* `filled_polygon` data (which goes stale
  the moment new copper is added without a GUI "Fill All Zones") could
  **not** be determined from Gerber inspection alone — a Gerber export may
  itself just plot the same stored data. Treat any zone-clearance DRC
  finding against newly-added copper as *likely real* but only fully
  resolvable by a live "Fill All Zones" (`B`) + re-DRC in the actual KiCad
  GUI.
- DRC exclusions in `.kicad_pro`'s `drc_exclusions` use a violation-specific
  hash format (`padstack|X|Y|uuid|uuid` for padstack findings — other
  finding types almost certainly use a different encoding). Do not
  hand-author a new exclusion entry by guessing the format; add it via the
  GUI's right-click "Exclude this violation" and let KiCad compute the
  hash, or leave the finding un-excluded and documented instead.

See [[feedback_kicad_hand_authoring]], [[feedback_generator_drift_and_freerouting]].

## `feedback_todo_stale_items.md`

---

---
name: feedback-todo-stale-items
description: "TODO.md checkboxes must be closed out the moment they become stale/resolved/inapplicable, not left open"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: e71f5b43-635b-43ab-97e8-bd3cad2cacfd
---

Never leave a TODO.md item as `- [ ]` (open) once its own body text shows it's been resolved, superseded, or is no longer applicable. Close it out (`- [x]`) with a short pointer to whatever resolved/superseded it, even if that resolution is a later note already sitting right below it in the same item.

**Why:** Caught 2026-07-04 — TODO.md §1.1.1.1 had an item ("Verify head-cargo mating boss positions in slicer") whose own inline text said "RESOLVED 2026-06-29 ... obsolete", but the checkbox itself was still unchecked. A stale open box next to a written resolution is misleading — a reader (or a future me) scanning for open work will treat it as still-actionable.

**How to apply:** Whenever editing/reviewing TODO.md (and especially during any full-file pass like a Rev-letter consolidation), scan for items whose body text contains resolution language ("RESOLVED", "SUPERSEDED", "DONE", "obsolete", "no longer applicable", "fixed by X") while the checkbox is still `[ ]`, and flip it to `[x]`. Don't wait to be asked per-item — this is a standing rule for any TODO.md touch, not a one-off cleanup task. Related: [project_r1_hull_frame_bake](project_r1_hull_frame_bake.md) (the specific stale item was in the hull-frame-bake joint-boss thread).

---

---
name: libreservo-kicad-primary
description: "LibreServo_v2-Sec — KiCad primary and fork version 4.0.0 as of 2026-08-04; EAGLE .sch/.brd frozen at v2.3.1 for backward compatibility only"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e52c4e2c-899d-43a5-acbf-f828b2878b2b
  modified: 2026-08-04T11:51:03.045Z
---

In `Griffing.tech/designs/LibreServo_v2-Sec`, **all new schematic and layout work goes in
`PCB/kicad/`**. Stated by the user 2026-08-04: EAGLE is end-of-life and unsupported, so the
EAGLE artefacts are kept **for backward compatibility only** — they are frozen legacy, not
the deliverable.

This **reverses** the 2026-08-03 position (EAGLE authoritative because the work was aimed at
an upstream LibreServo PR). Do not re-derive the old rule from `PCB/*.md` docs written before
this date; several still carry an "EAGLE is the standard" banner.

**The fork is version 4.0.0**, also set 2026-08-04. The user's reasoning: upstream shipped
v2.3.1 and had a v3 planned, and this fork goes past that v3's scope, so it takes the next
major number rather than colliding at v3.x. Applied to the **KiCad files only** —
`PCB/kicad/LibreServo-v4.0.0.*` plus the `.pretty` and `-eagle-import.kicad_sym` library
names, with `rev "4.0.0"` title blocks. The EAGLE files, the `Gerbers/` tree and the dead
STM32 firmware's `version_LS = 8` (an EEPROM protocol number, unrelated) all **keep their
old numbers deliberately**.

**How to apply:**

- Edit `PCB/kicad/LibreServo-v4.0.0.kicad_sch` / `.kicad_pcb`. Treat
  `PCB/LibreServo-v2.3.1.sch` / `.brd` as read-only history; do **not** back-port into them.
- `PCB/kicad/` is a KiCad 9.0.2 EAGLE import whose symbols live in
  `LibreServo-v4.0.0-eagle-import.kicad_sym` and carry **EAGLE symbol names, not deviceset
  names**. Search by reference designator, not part number.
- **Import defect to fix first:** the three EAGLE parts that had no package — `U1`, `U5`,
  `U6` — imported as **`#`-prefixed pseudo-components** (`#U1`, `#U5`, `#U6`), the same class
  KiCad uses for power flags, so they are not real board parts yet. `U1` also carries the
  **wrong part number**: symbol `MSPM0G3519`, value `M0G3519QRHBRQ1`; correct is
  `M0G3518QRHBRQ1` (the '3519 is not offered in RHB-32). The rest of the import *is* current
  with the EAGLE master, including the `CAN0_TX`/`CAN0_RX` rename.
- The old EAGLE "symbol-only deviceset" blocker (no package, no `<connects>`) is **dead**.
  Stock KiCad ships the right land patterns: `Package_DFN_QFN:Texas_RHB0032E_VQFN-32-1EP_
  5x5mm_P0.5mm_EP3.45x3.45mm` for `U1` (KLC-derived, pads 0.875 × 0.25 mm vs TI's 0.62 ×
  0.25 — outward-extended, not TI's literal pattern; pad 1 in the left column, correct
  orientation) and `Package_SO:SOIC-20W_7.5x12.8mm_P1.27mm` for `U5`/`U6`.
- Still genuinely open on the layout side, tool-independent: `U1`'s `.kicad_pcb` footprint is
  still the old `QFN32` at the STM32 placement, and `U5`/`U6` have no placement at all.

Related: [[libreservo-mcu-swap-chain]].

## `libreservo_mcu_swap_chain.md`

---

---
name: libreservo-mcu-swap-chain
description: "LibreServo_v2-Sec U1 MCU lineage — now TI MSPM0G3518-Q1 (M0G3518QRHBRQ1, VQFN-32 RHB); MSPM0G350x vs G351x security differ sharply"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f2609a6e-9649-4d8a-8a7c-eb7b7dcad915
  modified: 2026-08-04T11:01:11.465Z
---

`U1` on the LibreServo v2.3.1 board has been swapped repeatedly. Lineage, newest first:

**STM32F302K8U6 (orig, UFQFPN-32) → STM32G431 → NXP S32K144 (LQFP-48) → TI MSPM0G3507-Q1
→ TI MSPM0G3518-Q1** (`M0G3518QRHBRQ1`, VQFN-32 RHB, 5×5 mm) as of 2026-08-03.

Each pass has its own decision record in `PCB/`: `RS485-CANFD-TPM-upgrade.md`,
`S32K144-MCU-swap.md`, `MSPM0G3507-MCU-swap.md`, `MSPM0G3518-MCU-swap.md` (current).
Superseded docs are **kept with a banner**, not deleted — that is the repo's convention.

**The non-obvious trap:** MSPM0G**350x** and MSPM0G**351x** have very different security
silicon despite sharing the MSPM0 name, package and pinout. The '350x has *no* Customer
Secure Code (CSC), and without CSC there is no key store, no flash firewalls and no
monotonic counter. The '351x has CSC and therefore all of them. Authority is TI
**SLAAE29A** Table 1-2 (`M0G3x0x` column vs `M0Gx5 1x` column), local copy at
`Open-Secure-ESC/docs/datasheets/slaae29a.pdf`. Do not generalise "MSPM0 security" across
subfamilies. Datasheet **SLASFA6B** (`.../mspm0g3519-q1.pdf`) covers *both* G3518 and G3519.

**How to apply:** the '3507→'3518 swap moved no wires — the RHB-32 pad map is identical —
but the IOMUX `PINCM.PF` codes differ between the dies (e.g. `HFCLK_IN` 7→6, `TIMA0_C3`
5→8, `CAN0_TX/RX` 5/6→12). Pads staying put does not mean pin-mux config stays put.
Also: MSPM0 `NRST` **must** be pulled to VDD or the part never leaves reset, and `VCORE`
needs a dedicated 0.47 µF cap with nothing else on the net — both are new requirements
versus every earlier MCU on this board, which deliberately left reset unconnected.

Related: [[libreservo-kicad-primary]].

## `middle_section_inner_neck.md`

---

---
name: middle-section-inner-neck
description: Middle fuselage section is horseshoe ring PLUS a closed inner-neck tube (not just an open horseshoe)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: f7fafaed-76c7-4026-a266-87bc2f0e7ebe
---

The Serenity middle fuselage section (`airframe/stls/fuselage/middle_shell24_2mm_repaired.stl`,
hull Y +130.4..+203.6) is ONE printed piece comprising **two** structural elements, and it is a
recurring mistake to describe it as only the open horseshoe:

1. **Outer horseshoe ring** — U-shaped exterior frame, open at −Z (ventral). Its two lower arms
   continue aft as the landing skids into the rear section.
2. **Closed inner-neck tube** — a tube-like enclosed passage running the FULL length of the
   middle along the centreline (X ≈ −170 mm), connecting the cargo-bay interior to the rear
   engine-room interior, through the centre of the horseshoe, within the hull skin.

Confirmed by section analysis 2026-06-29: multiple closed nested contours centred on X≈−170
persist along Y (outer horseshoe shell + inner neck + skid-arm tubes).

**Why it matters structurally:** the closed inner neck is the natural full-perimeter tie
between cargo and rear (a full tubular splice IS feasible on the neck, unlike the open
horseshoe), and the continuous CF keel (CF-BAR-6X3) runs cargo→rear *through* the inner neck —
so "keel unsupported in foam through the middle" is a worst case; bonding the keel to the neck
wall is an available hard load path. Relevant to the cargo/middle and middle/rear joint design
(TODO §1.1.1.0b) and the keel re-evaluation. See [[head-cargo-splice-collar]].

**Why:** I described the middle as "open horseshoe, full-perimeter collar impossible" in a TODO;
the user corrected it — the inner neck (closed) makes that false. It is in CLAUDE.md but is easy
to forget. **How to apply:** when reasoning about middle-section joints/structure, always account
for the closed inner neck, not just the open horseshoe.

## `project_avionics_board_folder_reorg.md`

---

---
name: project_avionics_board_folder_reorg
description: "avionics/kicad/ reorganized one folder per board (Wash/Zoë/Emma/Kaylee/Jayne), each with kicads/scripts/gerbers subfolders — template is Kaylee"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 5907bd6b-3d6e-466a-84fb-aa2944f0f065
---

**Layout (established by user via the Kaylee folder, replicated 2026-07-13 to
Wash/Zoë/Emma/Jayne):** `avionics/kicad/<Board>/` contains:
- `<Board>.md` — design spec, at the folder root
- `kicads/` — `.kicad_pro`/`.kicad_sch`/`.kicad_pcb`/`.kicad_prl`
- `scripts/` — Python generator/modifier scripts (only if the board has any)
- `gerbers/` — production gerbers + drill file (only once fabricated)
- `<Board>-backups/` — KiCad autosave zips (gitignored via `*-backups/`)

Emma additionally keeps its `XCVR-49MHZ-2/` gerber subfolder name (renamed to `gerbers/`).
Jayne additionally keeps `Jayne.pretty/` (custom footprint lib) and `JAYNE_SOM_NETMAP.md`/
`Jayne_som_pinmap.csv` at the folder root (not under `kicads/`).

**Path-fixup gotcha (real bug this reorg introduces, fixed for Emma/Jayne 2026-07-13, NOT yet
fixed for Kaylee's own scripts):** any generator script using `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
to locate its own `.kicad_pcb`/`.kicad_sch`/footprint output was written when the script sat
flat in `avionics/kicad/<Board>/` — moving the script into `<Board>/scripts/` makes that `HERE`
one directory too deep. Every such script needs `HERE.parent` (for files now in `kicads/`,
one more `.parent` needed: `HERE.parent / "kicads" / ...`) or `HERE.parent.parent / "symbols"`
(for the shared `avionics/kicad/symbols/` dir). **`Kaylee/scripts/gen_kaylee.py` and
`gen_kaylee_pcb.py` still have this exact latent bug** (`here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent`
then `here / "Kaylee.kicad_pcb"`, which would now write into `Kaylee/scripts/` instead of
`Kaylee/kicads/` if re-run) — flagged to the user 2026-07-13, not fixed (Kaylee was described
as already "completed" and out of scope for that pass).

**Global `fp-lib-table`:** Jayne is the only board with a custom footprint library. It used to
live at `avionics/kicad/fp-lib-table` (adjacent to the old flat `.kicad_pro`); moved to
`avionics/kicad/Jayne/kicads/fp-lib-table` (adjacent to `Jayne.kicad_pro` post-reorg), with its
`uri` updated to `${KIPRJMOD}/../Jayne.pretty` to reach the `.pretty` dir one level up from

## `project_blender_nacelle_bore.md`

---

---
name: project-blender-nacelle-bore
description: Bug and fix in blender_nacelle_integrated_v2.py bore-center detection; correct bore centres for 50mm nacelles
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4311facf-577c-4c92-b5b8-50209bd78d38
---

## Bug: compute_bore_center used wrong initial centroid

`compute_bore_center()` in `blender_nacelle_integrated_v2.py` computed its initial
centroid as the mean of ALL vertices in the Z slice.  For the asymmetric Serenity nacelle
shells (pylon attach features, exterior skin asymmetry), this centroid drifted off the bore
axis.  Bore-wall vertices at R≈25 mm from the actual bore ended up outside the [19,31] mm
filter band, causing wrong ring points to be captured and the circle fit to return a bad center.

**Why:** The vertex centroid of an asymmetric hollow shell is NOT the bore axis.

**Fix applied 2026-05-26:** Changed the ring-point filter to use `expected_cx, expected_cy`
(the hardcoded bounding-box center) as the filter origin instead of the vertex mean.
Now finds ~5850 bore-wall pts per nacelle; refined center within 0.6 mm of fallback.

## Correct bore centres (1.25× scale, 50mm bore STLs)

Left  nacelle: X=42.50, Y=-190.01 (computed) | fallback X=42.75, Y=-190.625
Right nacelle: X=155.25, Y=-190.02 (computed) | fallback X=155.0, Y=-190.625

Both fallback values = bounding box XY centre of the respective STL.

## Script location and run command
```
cd thingverse-serenity
blender --background --python blender_nacelle_integrated_v2.py
```

Output: files-hollowed-18in/s_eng_{left,right}_stator_shell24_50mm.stl

Reconciling the Emma/Zoë PCB-ahead-of-schematic gap via a **schematic-first migration**
(schematic becomes source of truth, authored to match the as-placed PCB except for the
topology changes below). Driven by an auditable generator, gated on `kicad-cli sch erc` /
`pcb drc` (KiCad 9.0.2 on this machine; `sch erc` and `pcb drc` both supported headless).

**Baseline found 2026-07-04:** Emma.kicad_sch was a ~10-symbol EMI stub (J1/CMC/TVS/SMA/
C_X2Y only); Emma.kicad_pcb has 75 footprints / ~100 nets (full DDS+PA+LPF+LNA+AFSK RF
chain, UART/SBUS digital, RFM95W LoRa, 2nd ADIN1300 Ethernet PHY + T-ETH isolation, and the
full PB2-P1/P2 PocketBeagle passthrough bus). ERC baseline 64 warn; DRC baseline 256
violations + 94 unconnected. Zoë.kicad_sch is nearly complete (already has Conn_36 P1/P2,
RFM95W, all comms ICs) — its gap is small.

**User decisions (locked 2026-07-04):**
1. **Drop J1 (JST-GH-6P).** Honor root-CLAUDE.md "replace JST GH 6P with P1+P2 rails" intent
   over the lower-rework "keep J1" option. Modem UART rides PB2-P1 pin 15 (`UART_RCRS_RX`,
   =modem TX) / pin 16 (`UART_RCRS_TX`, =modem RX).
2. **PTT_N → repurposed PB2-P2 payload GPIO,** presence-gated by a cape-detect device-tree
   overlay (Emma has no MCU; fixed PB2 pinout has no spare GPIO). Provisional pad PB2-P2
   pin1 (SERVO7 ball). **Simon is payload-primary → his payload pads contend; River has
   slack.** Firmware/pinmux sign-off still owed.
3. **RSSI → 1-bit RSSI_DCD.** Analog can't ride the rail (AM62x GPADC = dedicated analog
   balls, not muxable onto digital pads). Add on-board comparator (RSSI_CMP, LMV331-class)
   thresholding RSSI_ANA; digital RSSI_DCD on a 2nd gated payload GPIO (prov. PB2-P2 pin2,
   SERVO6 ball). Analog RSSI_ANA kept as test point.

Tracked in TODO.md §1.2b (dated decision block). Working branch:
`emma-zoe-schematic-migration`. See [[project_jayne_cape_design]] for the sibling standalone
board (renamed from "Vera" to "Jayne", see [[project_jayne_vera_rename]]) and the PB2-I

1. **NCEES discipline pages do NOT name sponsoring societies.** The "Society of

   sponsorship to the society's own site, never to NCEES.
2. **No NCEES PE exam exists for aeronautical/aerospace engineering** (23
   disciplines, aeronautical absent). Statics & dynamics is **FE-level**, not a
   PE discipline. Both are documented as explicit exceptions in README.md.
3. **PE Electrical & Computer module is "Electronics, Controls, and
   Communications"** — not "Electrical and Electronics" as the top-level
   discipline list implies.

Verified from own sites: SFPE ("Licensing & PE Exam"), SNAME (PE Review Course).
**ISA role RESOLVED** at `isa.org/certification`: ISA "supports the Control
Systems Engineer (CSE) License" and offers review materials — it does NOT author
or administer the exam. Never upgrade that to "sponsors"/"develops".

ASTM/AIChE/AIAA return HTTP 403 to curl (anti-bot, links are real) → recorded
`VERIFIED (BLOCKED)`, not `VERIFIED`.

**Part 23 RESOLVED** — ecfr.gov WebFetch is blocked (302 to an unblock page);
use the eCFR API instead: `ecfr.gov/api/versioner/v1/full/<date>/title-14.xml?part=23`
(date must be <= the title's issue date). Findings: **§23.2230(b) DOES state the
1.5 FOS** — it is current text, my earlier caution was wrong. But **+3.8/-1.52
appear NOWHERE** in current Part 23 (§23.2200(b) is performance-based) — that
caution was right. §23.2265 "special factors of safety" covers articles with
"appreciable variability because of uncertainties in manufacturing processes" =
a real citation for printed-polymer allowables. See [[feedback-todo-stale-items]].

control-systems. CI enforces the mandatory qualified-review notice is present
and is the FIRST `##` section of every SKILL.md.

## `project_esc_mcu_swap_mspm0.md`

---

---
name: project_esc_mcu_swap_mspm0
description: "PENDING 2026-08-10 — Open-Secure-ESC MCU changes S32K144 to MSPM0G3518-Q1 for AES-256; VCORE gets a dedicated cap, NOT a slot-swap for VDDA"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: efb52d63-20b8-43e5-a772-41e6fa90b413
  modified: 2026-08-10T15:26:31.572Z
---

**Decided 2026-08-10, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.** The `Open-Secure-ESC` MCU changes
from NXP S32K144 to **TI MSPM0G3518-Q1**, package **PM (LQFP-64)**, orderable
**`M0G3518QPMRQ1`**. Reason (user): the S32K144's CSEc is SHE-compliant and
therefore **AES-128 only**; the MSPM0G351x has an **AES-128/256 accelerator
with GCM/CMAC** plus a 4-key keystore.

**Start from
`Open-Secure-ESC/docs/HANDOFF-mcu-swap-s32k144-to-mspm0g3518.md`** — it holds
every verified fact so nothing needs re-deriving. Mirrored as `TODO.md` §13.
Citations already exist: `[44]` = SLASFA6B datasheet, `[40]` = SLAAE29A
*Cybersecurity Enablers in MSPM0 MCUs* (the crypto reference the user supplied).

**The trap:** `VCORE` is NOT the equivalent of the S32K144's `VDDA`. VDDA is an
analog supply input tied to 3V3; VCORE is a regulator **output** — [44] p.52:
"The VCORE pin must only be connected to C_VCORE. Do not supply any voltage or
apply any external load to the VCORE pin." A slot-for-slot pin map would tie
VCORE to 3V3 and violate the datasheet. **User ruling: drop VDDA's rail
connection and give VCORE its own dedicated capacitor to VSS, nothing else on
that net.** The capacitance *value* stays `UNVERIFIED` — it is in a [44] p.51
table whose columns don't survive `pdftotext`; the ±20% tolerance IS verified.

Two consequences for `docs/secure-element-architecture.md`: finding **C-01**
(AES-128 ceiling) becomes RESOLVED and **C-05** (CSEc can't run at 112 MHz
HSRUN) no longer applies. **The OPTIGA Trust M's justification does NOT
change** — the MSPM0's AES engine is still symmetric, so the asymmetric
identity/key-agreement layer is still required. Preserve `SE_I2C_SCL` /
`SE_I2C_SDA` / `SE_RST` on the new symbol or the secure element silently
disconnects.

Related: [[project_optiga_trust_m_swap]], [[env_kiutils_missing]],
[[libreservo_mcu_swap_chain]], [[project_s32k144_pinout_source]]

## `project_fuselage_open_faces.md`

---

---
name: project_fuselage_open_faces
description: Fuselage splice-collar joints need OPEN mating faces; head-aft/middle-fwd were still capped — how they were opened and the collar Rev R3 rebuild
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 99ef4449-4dc8-48cc-bd28-6f7b82614978
  modified: 2026-07-28T02:14:02.114Z
---

2026-07-27: finished the four-section fuselage splice-collar joints (task: "one continuous, structurally sound fuselage").

**Capped-face gotcha (the crux).** The splice collars ([[project_rev_n_design_spec]]) require the section mating faces to be genuinely OPEN bores. `merge_cargo_interior.py` opens cargo and `regen_rear_interior.py` opens rear, but the published **head-aft (hull Y≈−71.2)** and **middle-fwd (Y≈+131.0)** shells were still CAPPED. `add_structural_features.MATING_PLANES`/`_flat_face_cutter` is a **no-op on an inward rounded closure that ends at the mate plane** (nothing "beyond" the plane to cut), so re-running it doesn't help. A cap shows up as a full-cross-section DISK in `collar∩shell` (~0.8–1.1k mm³) — no bond-gap or "waist" can clear it; only opening the face does. Detect with `mesh.contains` a mm inside the face, or a section-loop scan.

**Fix — `tools/open_mating_faces.py` (new, committed).** Two cap shapes → two methods: middle-fwd was a THIN FLAT MEMBRANE at the Y-extreme → cavity-PLUG subtraction (keeps wall rim + face location); head-aft was a ROUNDED necking closure → FLAT-CUT at the first genuinely-open station (bore 2 loops, inner>3000 mm²). **Opening head moved its mate plane inboard to hull Y = −72.95** (head now ends there; head/cargo gap ≈3.45 mm). Re-stamps the HULL-FRAME marker; idempotent.

**Collar generator = `generate_conforming_collars.py` Rev R3** (constant-profile, replaces + `git rm`s the three retired single-cross-section generators). profile = fwd_lap ∩ aft_lap (each a running intersection of that section's cavity over its 8 mm insertion span, inset BOND_GAP=1.0), extruded straight = ONE watertight ring, NO shell subtraction. A shell CLIP severs the thin 2 mm wall (splits the collar); a "waist" fragments unless WAIST_INSET<WALL_T. Residual `collar∩shell` (≤632 mm³) is a thin near-face wall-contact band (the processors cut "slightly-reduced still-open" faces) — advisory, eased with a chamfer at bond-up; joint boss pins were REMOVED 2026-07-06 (collar secures AND aligns). Masses head/cargo 14.4 g, cargo/middle 19.3 g, middle/rear 17.1 g.

**Cargo MESH-01 RESOLVED.** `merge_cargo_interior.py --repair-only`: reload the float32-exported STL, `merge_vertices` (weld boolean-seam duplicates), strip degenerate/duplicate faces, keep largest split body (its submesh re-weld closes the tiny seams), re-stamp — watertight single body, volume unchanged (298 576 mm³). All 59 STLs pass `tools/validate_stls.py`. Committed via harness auto-commit onto the working branch (PRs auto-merge).

## `project_fuselage_rev_t1c_tilt_drive.md`

---

---
name: project_fuselage_rev_t1c_tilt_drive
description: Rev T1c fuselage wing-root joint + multi-turn tilt actuator; the tenon forces the gear plane and costs an 18mm actuator standoff
metadata:
  type: project
---

2026-08-30, commit 16ebb59. Fuselage side of [[project_wing_rev_t1_fixed_spar]]
built in `merge_cargo_interior.py`: socket Y +21.00 / Z +66.85 / Ø20.4 / 18.5 mm,
boss Ø30.1, F688ZZ **and both tie rods deleted**, mortise 30.8→12.8, conduits
nav Ø4.2 @ Y+1.0 / AK7455 Ø7.5 @ Y+37.5 / shaft Ø4.4 @ Y+46.6.

**Three non-obvious forcings, in the order they bite:**

1. **Coaxial actuator does not fit.** DS3225 on the drive-shaft axis overlaps the
   Ø30.1 socket boss by 13.5 mm in Y at *either* output-shaft orientation.
   → fuselage spur pair m0.8 38T/38T, C 30.40, **1:1**.
2. **C is set by the landing-gear bay tops** (Z +82.39 + 3.0 budget ⇒ C ≥ 29.80).
   36T/37T fall under budget; 38T clears at 3.60 mm.
3. **The root TENON forces the gear plane, and this is the expensive one.** Tenon
   spans X −100…−108, Y +51.50…+63.50; its forward face is 4.90 mm from the shaft
   axis, so clearing it *in Y* needs a tip radius < 3.90 mm — no gear that can
   transmit at C = 30.40 qualifies. It must be cleared **axially**: mesh 11 mm
   inboard of X −100/−240, which costs an **18 mm actuator standoff** and
   18 mm/side of cargo-bay roof reach.

**Stage is 1:1 on purpose.** A step-up would trade the 48× torque surplus for
slew rate but pulls the actuator to 260° — under one revolution — re-opening the
180-vs-270 question Rev T1 exists to close.

**Root flange is a bonded PART, not printed hull.** Ray-cast 13×17 grid: the
sidewall skin moves **34.3 mm (port) / 37.0 mm (stbd)** across the 80×60
footprint. Filling to a plane ⇒ 34 mm thick; bounding with a plane ⇒ tangent to
the skin (0.46 mm non-manifold edge, 4 faces, at −86.33/+8.6/+52.2). Subtracting
a translated envelope from the full 900k-face shell was **worse** (4 boundary, 2
non-manifold, 4 bodies). Done **locally** on a cropped envelope it is clean:
`airframe/stls/fuselage/generate_wing_root_flange.py`, 12.7 g/side at 40 %.

Mass: **+77.0 g, +1.97 % AUW**; hover T/W was ~1.19 vs a 1.2 minimum → WA-R18
blocker.

Actuator = DS3225 + LibreServo_v4, pin removed, **multi-turn**, closed on the
AK7455 — same pattern as the cargo winch. Loop spec:
`docs/TILT_DRIVE_CONTROL_SPEC.md`. **The train is NOT self-locking and has no
holding provision (TILT-CTL-01/WA-R16) — flight-release blocker.**

## `project_generated_index_conflicts.md`

---

---
name: project_generated_index_conflicts
description: "PROJECT_INDEX.md/ARCHIVE_INDEX.md/tools/index_tags.json conflict on EVERY base movement; resolve by regenerating, never by picking a merge side. Since PR #183 the generator is deterministic (git-tracked only) so regenerating anywhere is safe"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 316a1d12-da5a-471d-b586-fa5585a88b3e
  modified: 2026-08-09T21:11:00.739Z
---

**STATUS UPDATE (PR #183, 2026-08-09): items 2 and 3 below are FIXED AT THE
SOURCE.** `tools/precommit_index.py` now filters `collect_files()` through
`git ls-files`, so its output is a deterministic function of the COMMIT.
Regenerating in a normal clone or a worktree is now safe and matches CI exactly,
and `--no-verify` is no longer needed for index commits. Item 1 (these files
conflict on every base movement) is UNCHANGED and still the main thing to know.
The history below is kept because it explains why the generator looks the way it
does — and because the fix only helps on commits that contain it.

The three generated artefacts — `PROJECT_INDEX.md`, `ARCHIVE_INDEX.md`,
`tools/index_tags.json` — are committed to git AND asserted by the CI check
"Project/Archive Index sync" (`tools/precommit_index.py --check`). Consequences
that cost real time on 2026-08-08/09 (PRs #178, #180, #181):

**1. They conflict on every base movement.** Any merge of `main` into a
long-lived branch conflicts in these files, repeatedly — PR #180 conflicted,
was fixed, then re-conflicted the moment #181 landed. **Never resolve by picking
a side** (`--ours`/`--theirs` is not a resolution here): neither side is
authoritative, the generator is. Take any side to get a tree, commit the merge,
then regenerate and commit that.

**2. Regenerate ONLY from a pristine `git archive` export.**
`collect_files()` walks the filesystem and **does not consult `.gitignore`**, so
regenerating in a normal working clone silently bakes in every untracked local
artefact. In this repo that was **154 files** (KiCad `*-backups/*.zip`, `~*.lck`
locks, `fp-info-cache`, sliced `airframe/gcode/`, `*.FCStd`). CI's fresh clone
has none of them, so the check fails forever. Recipe:
`git archive HEAD | tar -x -C $EXP && cd $EXP && python3 tools/precommit_index.py`
then copy the three files back.

**3. NEVER regenerate inside a `git worktree`.** `collect_files()` indexes every
root-level loose **file**, and a worktree's `.git` **is a file** (not a dir), so
it injects a bare `.git` index entry — the artefact removed in `48eae05`, which
recurred in 2026-08. The `.githooks` pre-commit hook re-runs the generator
in-place, so it re-adds `.git` even if you staged correct content: commit these
files with **`--no-verify`** when working from a worktree. (Hardening the
generator is tracked in TODO.md §1.1.3 — apply `IGNORE_DIR_NAMES` to the
root-level loop or filter to git-tracked paths.)

Verify before pushing by exporting the *resulting commit* and running
`tools/precommit_index.py --check` there — that is exactly what CI sees.
Related: [[project_nozzle_flap_shingle]] (the STL check that failed alongside it).

## `project_jayne_cape_design.md`

---

---
name: project_jayne_cape_design
description: Jayne cape (nose+cargo vision/ToF/laser board) architecture and the AI-brainstorm fact-check that shaped it
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e71f5b43-635b-43ab-97e8-bd3cad2cacfd
---

New board **"Jayne"** (Jayne's rifle) added 2026-07-03: one shared PCB design installed at two
locations — the bow sensor pod (nose) and the cargo bay nadir FPV mount (`cargo_fpv_bezel`).
Supersedes the RunCam Nano 4 analog camera (REF-SENSOR-001) originally in the bow sensor pod
design (TODO.md §1.1.1.1a). Full architecture in `avionics/CLAUDE.md` "Jayne" section; hardware
WBS at TODO.md §1.2c; firmware WBS at TODO.md §4.6.

**Important: Jayne is NOT a PocketBeagle 2 Industrial cape** (unlike Wash/Zoë/Emma). It's a
standalone, compact PCB with its own power input and processors, connecting to the rest of the
airframe only via the shielded JST-GH Ethernet ring and CAN-FD trunk connectors as a peer
network node — it does not use the P1+P2 header stack or mount onto a Wash/Zoë node. This was
corrected 2026-07-03 after an initial draft mistakenly called it a "cape" throughout
CLAUDE.md/avionics/CLAUDE.md/REFERENCES.md/TODO.md; all were fixed to say "board" and to state
the standalone relationship explicitly.

**Origin:** user imported a Gemini AI conversation exploring this board. The conversation
contained several fabricated/wrong claims that were caught by research before writing anything
into REFERENCES.md — logged in REFERENCES.md "Removed / Superseded Citations":
- TI DM38x (DaVinci DM385/DM388) + "remixed OpenIPC" was infeasible: DM38x is NRND, and
  OpenIPC's supported-hardware list contains no TI part at all (not even R&D-stage).
- LAN9355/KSZ9563 don't do HSR/PRP/MRP ring redundancy — Microchip's real part for that is
  **KSZ9477** (confirmed via app note AN3474).
- "ST33GTPMISPI" TPM part number doesn't exist.

**Resolved architecture:** TI AM62A3/AM62A7 (REF-SENSOR-003, real, in-production, MIPI
CSI-2 + ISP + H.264/H.265) running **TI's own open-source Linux BSP (V4L2/GStreamer)** —
explicitly not OpenIPC — for the vision half. Control half: TI MSPM0G3507 (REF-SENSOR-004,
native CAN-FD) + Infineon SLB9670 TPM (REF already used fleet-wide on all 8 Wash/Zoë nodes —
reused, not a new TPM part) + Microchip KSZ9477 (REF-SENSOR-005, real HSR/PRP) + TI
TCAN1042HG-Q1 (REF-SENSOR-006, note "HG" suffix required for 5 Mbps CAN-FD; plain
TCAN1042-Q1 is 2 Mbps only).

**Laser — REVISED 2026-07-05 to a single 520nm green source** (`docs/JAYNE_LASER_ANALYSIS.md`;
supersedes the earlier "different part per site" split). ONE green diode + driver serves both;
the two installs differ only in (1) a per-location terminal optic setting the SPREAD (nose
≈0.19°/3.3 mrad custom near-collimated; cargo ≈2.86°/50 mrad stock DOE or diverging dot — 15×
difference, set by the optic not the source) and (2) a per-location HARDWARE current limit
setting the POWER/class. **BOTH sites are Class 2 (≤1mW green) — the nose is NOT inherently
Class 3B** (corrected 2026-07-05 after user challenge). The Rev-A "nose 3B" was the worst-case
corner (power-diluted 2" spread crosshair + naked eye + full sun ≈ 82mW). Jayne's real
requirement is CAMERA visibility: a concentrated ~12mm green dot detected by Jayne's own strobed
camera + frame-difference needs only ~0.45mW → Class 2 (Class 1 with a narrowband filter).
Levers: (1) concentrate into a small dot not a 2" spread pattern (~18× area penalty avoided);
(2) camera strobe+difference detection drops the threshold from ~10% (eye) to ~1%. Cargo also
Class 2 (green 6.64× more luminous-efficient than the retired 650nm red). **Class 2 both sites
eliminates the Class 3B key-interlock AND mechanical shutter** — LASER_KEY_IN/LASER_IND become
optional defense-in-depth. Keep caps hardware-enforced. Nose Class 2 DEPENDS on firmware
strobe+difference in the AM62A7 ISP (TODO.md §4.6). 3B only returns if a human-at-the-50ft-target
must see a spread reticle in full sun (not Jayne's use case). Full derivation:
`docs/JAYNE_LASER_ANALYSIS.md` Rev A2. Green diode + optics not yet sourced (don't procure vs
placeholder).

**Laser is a thin-line CROSSHAIR (not a bare dot) = projected metrology reference** (Rev A2,
user requirement 2026-07-05): a PB2-I computes detected-object size + relative orientation from
ToF range + the crosshair's known projected angle + trig (size=(obj_px/cross_px)·2R·tan(θ/2);
tilt from arm foreshortening). Binding constraint = camera PIXEL COVERAGE, not power — the
nominal 2"@50ft crosshair is too small (~6px on a wide lens); size fan angle for ~24-48px
(nose ~4-8"@50ft or narrower FOV; cargo 3"@5ft already ample). Thin lines keep it Class 2
(~0.2-0.8mW). This corrected the Rev-A/A1 "prefer a bare dot" guidance. See §4.4.

**Jayne power — added 2026-07-05:** each board ≈1.2A typ/~2.1-2.7A peak @5V (AM62A7+KSZ9477+
camera+ToF+laser); the two boards get a **dedicated Kaylee 5V payload rail (U_BEC_JAYNE →
J_JAYNE)**, NOT the shared avionics bus (already near its dual-BEC single-fault capacity). Full
budget: `docs/POWER_DISTRIBUTION.md §3.2.1`. Kaylee KiCad change (U_BEC_JAYNE = 3rd TPS54620) not
yet implemented.

**Why this matters for future sessions:** if the user brings in another AI-assisted
brainstorm (Gemini, ChatGPT, etc.) for hardware design, fact-check every part number and
capability claim against real datasheets before writing it into REFERENCES.md/TODO.md/
CLAUDE.md — this session caught multiple fabricated claims that would have violated the
project's no-fabrication policy if copied through uncritically. See [[project_rev_n_design_spec]] for how this project's standards-vetting workflow generally operates.

## `project_jayne_som_carrier.md`

---

---
name: project_jayne_som_carrier
description: Jayne re-scoped to a PHYTEC phyCORE-AM62A SoM on a trapezoidal carrier; SoM 270-pad pinout is the one datasheet gate
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 25ab6e5c-252e-48fa-9ad6-63101a084097
---

**Jayne manufacturing path (locked 2026-07-11, user).** The raw-AM62A7 Jayne board was never
fabricable: 5 placeholder ICs, and NO LPDDR4/boot-flash/power-sequencing (an AM62A7 can't boot
without external LPDDR4). Resolution: mount the AM62A on a **SoM** and make Jayne a **carrier**
(deletes LPDDR4/flash/sequencing/DDR-BGA routing = readiness gaps G1/G2/G4 + most of G6). This
matches the fleet's PocketBeagle-2-module-on-cape pattern. See [[project_jayne_cape_design]].

**Module locked: PHYTEC phyCORE-AM62A** (40×40 mm, 270-pad 0.8 mm **direct-solder** edge — no
connector, no added Z-height). Verified: AM62A7 (AM62A74 quad-A53) + 2 TOPS; on-module 4 GB
LPDDR4 + 128 GB eMMC + 256 MB OSPI NOR; 2× GbE (1× DP83867 PHY + 1× RGMII to carrier), up to
9 UART / 3 CAN-FD / 6 I²C / 4 SPI, 1× 4-lane MIPI CSI-2. Rejected: Variscite VAR-SOM-AM62
(33 mm, plain AM62 = no ISP), Critical Link MitySOM-AM62A (~43 mm), Beacon AM62**L** (no
ISP/VPAC/encode). No AM62A SoM is ≤1 in wide (narrowest ~30 mm OSM).

**Form factor: TRAPEZOIDAL carrier** conforming to the nose cone — narrow end **≤ 25.4 mm
(1.0 in)** toward the sensor pod carrying camera/ToF/laser; widening aft to **≈ 42 mm** to seat
the module + KSZ9477. Length gated on nose interior aft of the pod (FreeCAD, refer to user).

**SnapMagic ToS (verified 2026-07-12):** SnapEDA Design Files are CC BY-**SA** 4.0 (§4.1) with
redistribution limits (§5.1); can't commit them to this CC BY 4.0 repo. So SnapEDA symbols/
footprints/STEP + vendor Eagle .lbr stay **gitignored**; we author **clean-room** symbols from
the factual pinouts (facts aren't copyrightable). Datasheet PDFs are kept in-repo (owner's call:
open/authoritative).

**ALL 5 clean-room symbols DONE (2026-07-12), each primary-sourced, loads in kicad-cli,
flake8+black clean, with a factual pinmap CSV:**
- `Jayne_SoM.kicad_sym` (270-pad, 7 banks) — `gen_jayne_som_symbol.py` from `jayne_som_pinmap.csv`.
- `Jayne_KSZ9477.kicad_sym` (129 = 128+EP) — `gen_jayne_ksz_symbol.py` from Microchip DS00002392C
  Table 3-1 (primary; SnapEDA symbol OMITTED pins 73/74/108=NC, so datasheet used).
- `Jayne_MSPM0G3507_RGZ.kicad_sym` (49) — TI SLASEX6C Fig 6-4; `gen_jayne_ic_symbols.py`.
- `Jayne_SLB9670_TPM.kicad_sym` (32) — Infineon DS Rev1.4 Tables 3/4/5; same generator.
- `Jayne_ISOW1044BDFMR.kicad_sym` (20) — TI SLLSFF7A Table 7-1; same generator.

**FLEET-WIDE FIX:** ISOW1044BDFMR is **20-pin DFM**, not "SOIC-16W" (TI SLLSFF7A). Corrected
avionics/CLAUDE.md + Jayne.md; TODO.md flags a fleet audit (Wash/Zoë footprints may be wrong).

**Footprints:** KSZ9477→`Package_QFP:TQFP-128_14x14mm_P0.4mm`, MSPM0→`QFN-48-1EP_7x7...`,
SLB9670→`QFN-32-1EP_5x5...` (KiCad std, EP sizes to confirm). **ISOW1044 DFM-20 land pattern
TBD** — isolation-critical (5kV), author from TI package drawing, don't substitute.

**REMAINING (the last phase):** integrate the 5 symbols into `gen_jayne.py` (replace raw AM62A7 +
U_PMIC + VDD_CORE/VDDR/VDDSHV), wire per `JAYNE_SOM_NETMAP.md`, ERC to 0. Challenge: SoM (7 units)
and KSZ (6 units) are multi-unit — wiring needs per-unit pin-coordinate math or GUI placement,
not gen_jayne.py's simplified glabel geometry. Pre-commit guard live
(`tools/precommit_kicad_load.py`). Full plan: `docs/JAYNE_MANUFACTURING_READINESS.md` Rev C.

## `project_jayne_som_endstate.md`

---

---
name: project_jayne_som_endstate
description: "Jayne (ex-Vera) vision board migrated to PCM-071 SoM end-state — real symbols/footprints, ERC 0, carrier rails added; pcbnew binding is broken"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1c62cfef-a8a5-4024-ac15-790b30813b27
---

Vera was renamed **Jayne** and moved into `avionics/kicad/Jayne/{kicads,scripts,Jayne.pretty}`
(part of a repo-wide per-board folder reorg: Wash/Zoë/Emma/Kaylee/Jayne each get their own
folder). On 2026-07-13 the board was taken from the placeholder-IC state to the **SoM
end-state**:

- Schematic `gen_Jayne_carrier_sch.py` instantiates REAL clean-room symbols (U_SOM
  `Jayne_SoM_PCM071` 240-pad, U2 KSZ9477, U3 MSPM0G3507, U4 ISOW1044BDFMR, U5 SLB9670), wired
  **by signal name** from each symbol's parsed pin table. **ERC = 0 errors.** Raw AM62A7 BGA +
  TPS65219 PMIC removed.
- PCB `gen_Jayne_carrier_pcb.py` places REAL footprints (0 placeholders), SoM on B.Cu; pad nets
  injected by a **text post-pass**; shelf-pack initial placement (no shorts). DRC parity clean
  bar 4 mounting-holes + TPM-EP GND tie. Remaining DRC = unrouted ratsnest + tight placement
  (user-reserved final placement + routing).

**Locked user decisions (2026-07-13):** (a) PCM-071 connector takes 5V in only, no rail back to
carrier (PHYTEC manual §5.1) → carrier makes its own rails: TLV62569 bucks (+3V3,+1V2) +
TLV75725 LDO (+2V5); (b) TPM + KSZ mgmt stay on MSPM0 SPI. RGMII SoM↔KSZ port6 is MAC-to-MAC
crossover. Regulator values / RGMII strap / MSPM0 pinmux are first-pass, verify before fab.

**Footprint facts:** ISOW1044BDFMR is 20-pin DFM = `Package_SO:SOIC-20W_7.5x12.8mm_P1.27mm`
(NOT SOIC-16W — old error). KSZ9477 needed a custom `Jayne:TQFP-128-1EP_…EP10x10` (generic
TQFP-128 + datasheet 10×10 GND EP as pad 129). Wurth 749010012A transformer footprint was
extracted from the old board (no library file exists) into Jayne.pretty.

**Tooling landmine:** the sandbox pcbnew 9.0.2 Python binding is broken — `FootprintLoad` after
`board.Remove()` segfaults; `Pads()`/`FindPadByNumber()` return unwrapped `SwigPyObject`s with
no `.SetNet`; `SaveBoard` prunes zero-pad nets. Workaround: load all footprints before any
Remove, and inject pad nets + rebuild the net table in a text pass. Full write-up:
`avionics/kicad/Jayne/PCBNEW_SWIG_BUG.md`. See also [[project_vera_som_carrier]],
[[project_vera_cape_design]].

## `project_landing_gear_r6_variants.md`

---

---
name: project-landing-gear-r6-variants
description: "Rev R6 canonical articulated landing leg now ships as two leg-length variants (1.5in default, 3.0in extended/kept) sharing one bay/foot/wire BOM"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8d7a83fc-067e-4887-ad99-15b4a8a6dd5c
  modified: 2026-07-26T18:17:13.679Z
---

The Rev R6 landing gear (canonical articulated hip-pivot leg, replacing
the Rev R5 rigid vertical post) is split into two leg-length variants as
of 2026-07-23, per [[feedback_ground_clearance_requirement]]:

- **`canonical_leg_r6_1_5in.scad`** — 1.5 in (38.1 mm) belly clearance,
  **default**, wired into `airframe/FreeCAD-scripts/serenity_assembly.py`.
- **`canonical_leg_r6_3_0in.scad`** — 3.0 in (80 mm) belly clearance,
  **extended, kept** (not scrapped) for rough-field/extra-margin missions.
  This is the original 2026-07-21 Rev R6 design point.

Both share **identical bay, foot, and wire geometry** (confirmed
byte-for-byte via STL volume/bounds comparison) — only the leg-frame
`KNEE`/`ANKLE`/`GROUND_Z`/`R_H` skeleton constants differ. STL naming:
`lg_r6_1_5in_*.stl`, `lg_r6_3_0in_*.stl` for variant-dependent parts
(leg_frame, leg_assembled, leg_deformed, hull_legs, hull_stance);
`lg_r6_common_*.stl` for the shared bay/foot/wire parts — all in
`airframe/stls/fuselage/landing-gear/`.

**Key physics (both variants reuse the SAME wire hardware, solved once
against the 3.0in lever):** shortening the leg trades ground clearance for
higher peak deceleration, since ground force F = 2·P·r/R_h is inversely
proportional to the hip→foot arm R_h, while wire stroke (and hence hip
bending moment M = 2·P·r, and thus leg-frame structural margin) is
R_h-independent. At the 6 ft drop schedule: 1.5in runs 81 g tail-down /
162 g level with 15.5 mm residual clearance (no margin for a
single-ductile-wire-only arrest); 3.0in runs 52 g / 104 g with 44.9 mm
residual. Full numbers: `tools/landing_gear_r6_sizing.py` (parameterized
by `LEG_VARIANTS` dict) and `docs/LANDING_GEAR_ANALYSIS.md` Rev R6 §4.7.

The original undifferentiated `canonical_leg_r6.scad` (byte-identical to
the 3.0in variant) was retired and archived to
`archives/airframe-archives/archive/openscad/fuselage/` when the split was
made explicit.

**Open:** LG-17 (6 ft vs 4 ft ductile wire diameter, orthogonal to the
leg-length choice), LG-10 (bay flank-conforming bake), LG-18
(mass-reduction, targets differ per variant: ≤300 g for 1.5in / ≤350 g for
3.0in).

## `project_lg_sponson_wells.md`

---

---
name: project-lg-sponson-wells
description: "Rev R6 gear bays mount on the sponson's 25° angled panel (NOT the cargo flank); LG-10 CLOSED 2026-08-17 — bay seat is a shared per-station DATUM, not a conforming patch"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  modified: 2026-08-17T00:00:00.000Z
---

Landing-gear/hull integration. **LG-10 closed 2026-08-17**, all eight sub-items.
The canonical `cargo_sect_shell24_2mm_repaired.stl` IS now published (an older
version of this note said it was untouched — that was already stale).

**The mounting face is the sponson's 25° angled panel, not the cargo flank.**
Wrong for the whole of Rev R6; it caused every defect found.

- Measured panel normal **(0.901, 0.015, −0.433) port**, mirrored stbd; tilt
  25.1–26.0°. Use this constant directly — a per-station frame search lands on
  door-frame/joint surfaces and returns junk normals. Since LG-10.3 it only
  LOCATES the opening; it never orients the mount (bolt axis vs panel normal
  disagree by a 21–24° yaw no `BAY_CANT` can remove).
- **Y −7 is where the sponson meets the wall**, so the wells need NO sponson
  extension. A convex-hull extension was tried and reverted: +61.7 g for
  nothing.

**How the bay actually seats (LG-10.6 — the big one).** The conforming hull
patch and `BAY_CONFORM` were **retired, not built**. The hull-side flange
rebate (flat trapezoidal pocket, 5 mm deep, 12 mm into the skin) already shaves
the whole footprint, so the hull presents a FLAT seat normal to the bolt axis;
cutting the printed part to a curve would put the mismatch back and split the
bay into four unshared geometries. The real defect was the **datum**:
`BAY_STANDOFF` was 12.6/5.4 (measured along the panel NORMAL) against a pocket
cut at −7.69/−3.55 in the plate frame — a **3.5–7.7 mm air gap under every M3**.
Now **4.91 fore / 1.85 aft**, ONE datum per station (the deeper corner), which
is what keeps the §11.4 shared-BOM claim true. Single-sourced as
`merge_cargo_interior.station_seat_data()`; gated by
`tools/landing_gear_bay_seat_fit.py` — re-run after ANY hull re-merge.

**LG-10.8 was not about the feet.** All four are level to 0.0000 mm. The
assembly's lowest point was not the sole: a hardcoded spigot cube drove the
ankle spigot **2.9 mm through the foot** on the 1.5in leg (743.9 mm³ of leg
inside the foot — unassemblable). The rule, stated in `FOOT_HUB_H`'s own
comment: `ANKLE[2] = GROUND_Z + ANKLE_DISC_D/2 + FOOT_HUB_H` (= +18). The 3.0in
leg satisfied it; the 1.5in was 6.4 mm short from the variant split. Fixed by
moving ANKLE (−64.5 → −58.1), NOT `GROUND_Z` (pinned by the 1.5 in spec) and
NOT `R_H` (which is what keeps the LG-17 load schedule valid). In-SCAD
`assert()` guards it now; `tools/landing_gear_foot_stance.py` gates it.

**Two latent bugs found on the way:**

1. **`bowed_wire` in `canonical_leg_r6_1_5in.scad`** built its side wall as a
   list of face PAIRS inside a **no-op `concat()`** (the 3.0in file always had
   the correct `each`). Every wire on the DEFAULT leg exported as 20 cap faces
   of zero volume; nobody noticed because the shared wire STLs came from the
   other file. Moral: compare shared parts GEOMETRICALLY across variants —
   `tools/export_landing_gear_stls.py` now does.
2. **Zero-area collinear slits.** A 0.02 mm collar nudge created a coplanar
   boolean seam and a 3-edge boundary loop 0.25 mm long that failed CI.
   `trimesh.repair.fill_holes` CANNOT close one (the fill triangle has zero
   area and is rejected); collapsing the loop can.
   `merge_cargo_interior.close_zero_area_slits()` does it, only for loops
   flatter than 1 µm, so real holes still fail loudly.

**Traps that cost real time:** an edit can silently not apply and still print
`RESULT: PASS` / `CI_valid=True` — assert replacements and confirm the volume
moved. "Most outboard vertex" finds the hull's widest point (Z ≈ 78), not the
bay station (Z 38). `nx > 0.7` also catches the starboard INNER wall — add an
X-vs-centreline constraint. And **measuring the seat on the published shell is
circular** (the rebate is already cut there) — measure on `BLENDER_SRC`.

Still open: procurement/test only — LG-15/LG-16 block leg fab, LG-13 blocks
first flight. Carried: the **4× stroke-formula error** in
`wire_stroke_available()` (`H_DEF_DUCT` should be 9.9 not 19.2; ductile stock
75 → ~40 mm, ~33 g) — correcting it re-opens LG-15 and shrinks the bay.
Known noise: `landing_gear_cowl_clearance.py --variant 1_5in` reports 5.468 mm³
at 26°, which is 4° PAST the 22° stop; pre-existing, clear through the real
stroke.

See [[env_venv_hides_system_python]] — all this tooling needs
`/usr/bin/python3` for manifold3d. Related: [[cargo_interior_merge_pipeline]],
[[project_landing_gear_r6_variants]], [[project_wing_spar_rev_s1b]].

  deleting the gear train alone left the pivot ~unchanged, but the Rev T2 40 mm

  (66 STLs pass validate). FIRST-PASS band ≈109–112 (densities pending sliced

  `PINION_A_Z` tracks `PIVOT_Z`. Open follow-ups (root TODO §1.1.3): single-

  stator teardrop-strut aero VERIFY (kept 11 vanes — coprime w/ 12-blade rotor,
  Tyler–Sofrin), and the Ø72-pocket eating the aft cowl tail (shell now ends duct
  Z≈172 vs 185). See [[project_rev_n_design_spec]].
- **Idler axial mesh-band fix (user decision):** Crown Pinion offset 10 mm toward
  intake — `CROWN_Z = NOZZLE_RING_Z − 10 = 156.25`, decoupled from the nozzle
  station. Idler seated in `serenity_assembly.py` at `Z = CROWN_Z − 6` (Idler-In

## `project_nacelle_gear_train_r1_findings.md`

---

---
name: project-nacelle-gear-train-r1-findings
description: "Rev R1 nacelle idler-gear axial mismatch and cargo_sect_shell24.scad port/stbd mirroring bug found 2026-06-22 while completing TODO.md §1.1.3 — both open, both need user decision"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e7217d68-ebd9-41bb-914f-9fef78b29a32
---

While completing TODO.md §1.1.3 (Nacelles) on 2026-06-22 — openscad, blender,
and the trimesh Python module became available in the dev environment for the
first time, unblocking several previously-stalled render/verify tasks — two
new structural design issues were found that are NOT yet fixed:

**1. Idler axial mesh-band mismatch (nacelle_nozzle_idler.scad).** The new
Crown-Pinion-to-ring idler gear (added earlier the same day to resolve a
radius mismatch — see [[project_r1_hull_frame_bake]] for the surrounding
nacelle hull-frame context) has its two gear sections (Idler-In, Idler-Out)
10 mm apart axially. But Crown Pinion and the Nozzle Ring it must
simultaneously mesh are both defined at the exact same Z station (`CROWN_Z`
= `NOZZLE_RING_Z`, identical value, 166.25 mm) — zero mm apart. A single
idler shaft can't present two sections 10 mm apart and mesh two targets 0 mm
apart. Needs a decision: move Crown Pinion's Z, or change the idler's
internal `GEAR_GAP`/section order. The idler's angular position WAS solved
(50.9° off local +X, two mirror solutions per a triangle-inequality check)
and is committed; only the axial (Z) placement is still a placeholder in
`serenity_assembly.py` (`CROWN_Z - 11.0`, explicitly flagged VERIFY).

**2. cargo_sect_shell24.scad mirrors port/stbd across the wrong axis.** The
file's own header defines local Z as vertical/dorsal (matches hull frame,
`hull_Z = local_Z` in the bake transform) — but three features
(`nacelle_servo_mount_block(z_sign)`, `wing_root_mortise(z_sign)`,
`spar_bearing_block(z_sign)`) all label their `z_sign=+1`/`-1` cases "port
wall"/"stbd wall" while mirroring across Z (vertical), not X (lateral, the
actual port/stbd axis). Concretely, `nacelle_servo_mount_block(+1)` and
`(-1)` use identical X/Y and differ only in Z — both pads land at the same
lateral position, one near the bay's dorsal interior face and one near its
ventral face, neither "toward" either nacelle. The same `z_sign` pattern is
reused for the wing-root mortise and spar bearing block — both load-bearing,
not cosmetic. Not fixed: flagged for user review given the structural
stakes, per CLAUDE.md's "ask the user for manual placement" guidance on
complex/uncertain geometry.

**Also resolved cleanly that day (no open question):**
- `crown_pinion_boss()` in `nacelle_pod_50mm_tandem.scad` had a copy-paste
  `rotate([0,90,0])` bug (copied from `pinion_a_boss()`) contradicting two
  other files' own documentation that Crown Pinion is Z-axis/longitudinal.
  Fixed by removing the rotation.
- Sector-gear standoff (`NACELLE_FACE_X_PYLON = 34.0 mm` in
  `serenity_assembly.py`) was assumed to be an unconfirmed guess (no tilt
  bracket SCAD found) — actually `wing_nacelle_pylon_revo.scad` IS the tilt
  bracket, and `nacelle_pod_50mm_tandem.scad`'s own `NACELLE_FACE_X_PYLON`
  constant (also 34.0 mm) is documented as taken from real STL measurements,
  confirming the value already in use. (The pylon file's own simplified
  ellipse model gives 30.25 mm instead — a separate, lower-priority
  reconciliation noted but not done.)
- Tip cap (`nacelle_tip_cap_port/stbd.stl`) has no SCAD source; investigated
  the existing placeholder STL (simple OD80/ID70/8mm annulus, geometrically
  trivial) but did NOT author a replacement — its functional purpose
  (bearing cap? aero fairing? hatch?) isn't documented anywhere, so a
  parametric model can't be written responsibly without asking the user.

See `TODO.md` §1.1.3.3 for the full write-up of all of the above.
